source.quote: Chord Electronics' own product page for DAVE, read 2026-11-24, Technical Spec: « 4x 75Ω S/PDIF BNC Coax - 44.1kHz to 384kHz », « 1x AES XLR - 44.1kHz to 96kHz », « 2x Fibre Optic TOSLINK - 44.1kHz to 96kHz », « 1x USB Type B - 44.1kHz to 768kHz (16 - 32bit) - PCM and DSD ». « Sample frequencies: 44.1Khz - 768Khz (16 - 32bit) and DSD64 to DSD512 native DSD + DoP (input dependant) ». « At its heart lies the advanced Spartan 6 Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) », « Tap length filter: 164,000 ». Title: « Reference-level Digital to Analogue Converter, Headphone Amplifier and Preamplifier ».

facts.chip: No commercial converter: « the advanced Spartan 6 Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) », with « Tap length filter: 164,000 » - more than three times the Qutest's 49,152 on the same maker's own scale.

_two_contradictions_inside_the_maker: THE PAGE DISAGREES WITH ITSELF: its spec row reads « 4x 75Ω S/PDIF BNC Coax - 44.1kHz to 384kHz » while its own Key Features icon reads « 4x 768kHz BNC Coax Inputs ». The specific row is recorded. AND THE MANUAL DISAGREES WITH THE PAGE on AES: the page says « 1x AES XLR - 44.1kHz to 96kHz » and the DAVE User manual V1.4 says « AES input 44. 1 kHz t o 19 2kHz (under AES s tandard... » - the same shape of disagreement as the Qutest's optical input, on a different input of a different device. Two devices, two page-against-manual contradictions, one maker. That is a pattern and not an accident.
_what_is_not_asserted: Bit depth for coax, AES and optical: the page states it only for USB. The « DXO » expandable input is listed with no rate, so nothing is claimed for it. « input dependant » on the DSD line is not explained by the maker, so native_dsd and dop are recorded at device level where the source puts them and NOT pushed down into the inputs.
